messages:
Samir: quick ping — I'm rolling an experiment on canary-3 to test autoscale prefetch smoothing + KV key bucketing. Goal: reduce oscillation during bursty autoscale events without prewarming every instance. details below.
Tess: +1 can you add sim traces? curious about tail latency impact.
mike_r: what's the exact change to keying? last time bucket mismatch caused skewed hit rates.
Samir: good call. basic idea: instead of exact-prefix keys we hash the first N tokens into 128 buckets, then prefetch top-K per bucket during scale-up. helps avoid huge fanout when many unique prefixes.
benji: hashing sounds fine but what about collisions causing wrong KV reuse between contexts? could poison outputs.
Samir: collisions are expected but we keep bucket size small and always validate generation prefix match before using KV. fallback to cold path if mismatch. safety check: 
```
if kv.meta.prefix_token_id != request.prefix_token_id:
  use_cold_path()
```
Tess: how are you smoothing autoscale triggers? we get noisy up/down churn around thresholds.
Samir: we add a scaled moving-average on observed qps with two windows (10s fast, 120s slow). only trigger prefetch when fast > up_threshold AND fast > slow * 1.15. similarly, we don't tear down prefetch for 90s after scale-down event.
mike_r: sounds decent. please surface metrics: prefetch_latency, prefetch_hit_rate_by_bucket, prefix_mismatch_rate, and simulated_output_regressions.
deploy-bot: canary job started (job_id: job-87c4). snapshot: model=v2.7, quant=4bit, nodes=3.
Samir: FYI infra-sim-bot will run synthetic traffic with bursty poisson traces + user-like prefix distributions. sim job id: sim-00421.
infra-sim-bot: sim-00421: phase1 (baseline) completed — 30m, 100k requests, baseline hit_rate: 38%, p95 latency: 128ms.
infra-sim-bot: sim-00421: phase2 (hash-bucket prefetch) completed — 30m, 100k requests, hit_rate: 63%, p95 latency: 142ms, prefix_mismatch: 0.07%
benji: hit_rate improvement is good. p95 regressed 14ms — acceptable? what's the added CPU/IPC on the runtime?
Samir: we see ~8% CPU increase on runtime side for prefetch workers, and ~1.2x memory used for cached KV shards. tradeoff looks cost-positive for most mid-tail workloads.
Tess: can we reduce p95 by async prefetch with priority for active requests? e.g., prefetch first tier synchronously, rest async.
Samir: plan: two-tier prefetch. immediate K=2 per bucket blocking, then background fill up to K=6. updating canary now with that tweak.
mike_r: also add metric for prefetch_backpressure (queue length) so autoscaler doesn't count prefetch inflight as real capacity.
Samir: good call. added.
infra-sim-bot: sim-00421b (two-tier) done — hit_rate: 60%, p95 latency: 130ms, prefix_mismatch: 0.05%, prefetch_cpu +5% vs baseline.
benji: two-tier looks like the sweet spot. want to run a small production canary for 6 hours with gradual ramp.
Tess: agree, but add a regression check: compare generation distributions on eval set to detect subtle output drift. if KL > 0.01 abort.
Samir: added KL check and auto-rollback hook. scheduling prod-canary job now.
deploy-bot: prod-canary scheduled (canary-21), ramp=0->10% over 30m, monitoring windows: 5m, alert if any metric delta > threshold.
mike_r: FYI we should gate this behind the per-account SLA tier — don't prefetch for free-tier tenants by default.
Samir: done, feature flag: prefetch.tiered_by_account = true. will only enable for paid+internal.
Tess: anything else? docs + runbook for oncall if prefetch floods nodes?
Samir: adding a small runbook: how to disable feature flag quickly, and a script to flush prefetch queues: `./infra/ops/flush_prefetch.sh canary-21`
benji: nice. thanks team. will review sim logs and open a PR for the runbook.
Samir: thanks — will post follow-up with final numbers once prod-canary completes. :ship:
